drafts.title: Displays (HUD and center screen) remain readable in bright sunlight
drafts.description: Customers can read critical information on the head-up display (HUD) and center screen in bright sunlight without having to shade the display or change viewing angle.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a standardized sunlight test (direct sunlight, 1000–1100 lux at 60° incidence), HUD symbology and center-screen primary UI elements (navigation directions, speed, climate status) must be legible from driver seating position in 9 out of 10 trials; measured contrast ratio and perceived glare must result in a legibility score ≥90% vs. a calibrated visibility panel.
assumptions: Standardized visibility test method and calibrated panels are available for supplier validation.
HUD and screen optical coatings and brightness control can be tuned within existing automotive hardware constraints.
uncertainties: Some extreme phone reflections or aftermarket screen protectors may still cause local glare not covered by the standardized test.

drafts.title: Tactile physical controls for temperature and fan speed operable without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can adjust cabin temperature and fan speed by feel so they do not need to look at the screen or take eyes off the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A blind usability test (driver keeps eyes on road) must allow users to set a target temperature within ±1°C and change fan speed by at least two levels within 5 seconds in 9 out of 10 attempts.
assumptions: Physical controls can be integrated without significantly increasing center console clutter.
User testing will use a representative sample of drivers (age and hand size variation).
uncertainties: Some drivers will still prefer touch control for aesthetic or secondary adjustments.

drafts.title: Reliable natural-language voice control with high in-vehicle accuracy
drafts.description: Voice control recognizes and executes common driving commands reliably so drivers can keep hands on the wheel and eyes on the road.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under realistic driving noise (wind/road noise up to 70 dB(A)), the voice system must correctly understand and execute 95% of a standardized set of 150 common driving commands (navigation destinations, climate, media, phone) in 20 test users across 3 accents.
assumptions: Testing uses a standardized command set representative of customer phrasing.
Onboard language models and microphone placement will be optimized during development.
uncertainties: Extreme accents or very noisy aftermarket audio environments may reduce accuracy below the target.

drafts.title: Wireless phone charging works reliably for common phones during normal drives
drafts.description: When a compatible phone is placed correctly on the pad, charging continues without unexpected interruptions for the duration of typical drives.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across a compatibility test matrix of the top 10 phone models by US market share, wireless charging sessions must remain active (no interruption >2 seconds) for 95% of 2-hour continuous-driving tests and must deliver charge increase of ≥10% for phones starting at 20% battery.
assumptions: Test phones are placed according to user guidance; phone cases thicker than 3 mm or metallic cases are excluded from pass criteria or noted.
Tests include realistic vehicle vibration and temperature conditions.
uncertainties: Some third-party phone cases, accessories, or phone firmware updates could cause incompatibilities not captured in the initial matrix.

drafts.title: Driver profile storage and controls meet GDPR data-subject rights
drafts.description: Customers can review, export, and delete personal driver profile data and see consent logs so the driver profile satisfies GDPR data-storage and access requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The vehicle user interface and connected portal must allow the data subject to (a) export a complete machine-readable copy of their driver profile, (b) request deletion of personal profile data, and (c) view an auditable consent log — each action must complete or be acknowledged within 48 hours; retention and processing controls must match GDPR requirements in documented data flow.
assumptions: Necessary backend processes and regional data handling policies will be implemented before launch.
Legal review will define exact storage duration and localization per market.
uncertainties: Non-EU markets may have differing requirements that need separate implementation.
Third-party services integrated with profiles may have different data handling constraints.

drafts.title: Infotainment software prepared for China certification (CCC) at launch
drafts.description: The infotainment stack is implemented so it can pass Chinese CCC certification and be delivered as a market variant for China.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Infotainment build for the China market must achieve CCC certification clearance (formal certificate issued) before vehicle delivery in China; no China-market sales rollout will occur without the certificate.
assumptions: Regulatory submission timelines and testing labs are available for the planned launch window.
Localization and any region-specific feature adjustments will be scoped into the China build.
uncertainties: Certification timelines can change due to regulatory updates or additional testing requirements.

drafts.title: More affordable and transparent pricing, packages and ownership offers
drafts.description: Customers see clearer, more competitive pricing: an affordable base model, common cold-weather features included or reasonably priced, transparent dealer markup, and market-competitive lease/finance options (including optional subscriptions).
drafts.acceptance_criterion: When the successor launches in the US: (a) an entry 5 Series model MSRP < $50,000, (b) a manufacturer-backed lease option for the entry model that is at least $50/month lower than the comparable Mercedes E-Class lease in the same region, (c) 0% APR financing available for up to 12 months on at least two popular trims, (d) heated seats offered as a subscription at $15/month with monthly cancel, (e) heated steering wheel included as standard in the Cold Weather package on at least one popular trim, (f) Comfort package price reduced by 30% vs. the current model's Comfort package, and (g) dealer markup on factory-installed options capped at 5% above MSRP or clearly disclosed at point of sale.
assumptions: Manufacturer and dealer agreements can be adjusted to implement capped markups and new package pricing.
Competitive lease and finance targets are measured against the equivalent Mercedes E-Class offering in the same retail region and launch period.
Some content changes (e.g., which features are standard on which trims) are acceptable to meet the MSRP and package targets.
uncertainties: Market inflation, materials cost changes, or supply constraints could affect final MSRP and package pricing.
Dealer network cooperation is needed to implement markup caps and transparent disclosures.

drafts.title: Customer request for a specific cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) — engineering spec (out of scope)
drafts.description: Some customers specifically requested that the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip. This is a hardware component request rather than a direct customer-facing outcome.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: N/A — engineering component request. If implemented, acceptance criteria must be defined by HW performance and supplier validation plans.
assumptions: Customers equate a specific chip name with perceived performance; actual performance can be achieved by multiple hardware configurations.
uncertainties: Availability, supplier contracts, and platform compatibility for a specific chip cannot be guaranteed at product launch.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an engineering-level specification naming a chipset. Customer-facing outcomes (responsiveness, UI performance) should be specified instead; chipset choice is an engineering decision.
